title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Climate Trigger) Bill 2022
short_title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Climate Trigger) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would amend the EPBC Act to add a climate trigger, requiring assessment of projects that emit large amounts of greenhouse gases.

The bill would create a new class of controlled action for greenhouse gas emissions, with two thresholds: projects emitting 25,000 to 100,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent scope 1 emissions per year would need ministerial consideration under Part 9, while those emitting above 100,000 tonnes would be rejected like nuclear projects.

The Climate Change Authority would have to develop a national carbon budget to 2050 and update it annually, and the minister must use that budget when deciding approvals, strategic assessments, conservation agreements, and bioregional plans.
changes: Establishes a new controlled action class for greenhouse gas emissions under the EPBC Act.
Creates two thresholds for emissions: 25,000 to 100,000 tonnes per year triggers ministerial consideration, and above 100,000 tonnes forces rejection.
Requires the Climate Change Authority to set a national carbon budget to 2050 and assess it yearly.
Forces the minister to consider the carbon budget and emissions targets when approving projects, entering conservation agreements, and developing bioregional plans.
Prohibits the minister from using alternative approval processes for actions with a significant impact on emissions, except under Part 10.
summary.affected: Proponents of emissions-intensive projects, the Minister for the Environment, and the Climate Change Authority.
